model_scope: Applies to isolated neutron stars with magnetic-dipole spin-down and dense-matter phase transitions; excludes binary recycling and companion-ablation evolution. Observables are surface temperature and bolometric X-ray luminosity versus age for baseline cooling, spin-down-induced phase-transition cooling, and phase-transition cooling with superfluid suppression.

scientific_question: How does the surface temperature evolution differ between massive neutron stars undergoing spin-down induced core compression and those without, and can this distinguish the phase-transition mechanism from baseline cooling?
symbolic_constraints: The ODE_IVP state variables are core temperature, surface temperature, central density, moment of inertia, and spin frequency.
Initial conditions must be consistent with the selected mass, radius, EOS, initial central density, initial spin period, and initial spin frequency.
Spin-down-induced core compression may activate the phase transition only when central density reaches the critical density within the assumed transition width.
Latent heat release is included only in scenarios where the phase-transition volume fraction is active.
Superfluid suppression of neutrino emissivity is included only in Scenario C.
Scenario A disables phase-transition latent heat and superfluid suppression while retaining baseline neutrino cooling.
Scenario B enables spin-down-induced phase-transition latent heat without superfluid suppression.
Scenario C enables spin-down-induced phase-transition latent heat and superfluid suppression.
All temperatures and densities are non-negative.
Spin frequency decreases monotonically under the assumed isolated magnetic-dipole braking law.
Moment of inertia changes only through spin-down-induced core compression and phase transition, not through mass loss or binary accretion.
Surface boundary conditions are coupled to radiative transfer without embedding numerical atmosphere constants in the symbolic model.
EOS parameters and phase-transition parameters must be drawn from a single self-consistent dense-matter EOS family.
Initial spin frequency must be consistent with initial spin period.
Simulation age must be measured from the initial condition.
symbolic_model_intent: Construct an ODE_IVP for core temperature evolution coupled to spin frequency, moment of inertia, central density, phase-transition latent heat, heat capacity, neutrino emissivity, thermal conductivity, and a surface radiative boundary condition. The symbolic model compares baseline cooling, spin-down-induced phase-transition cooling, and phase-transition cooling with superfluid suppression.
title: Thermal Signatures of Phase Transitions in Massive Neutron Stars: Distinguishing Spin-Down Induced Core Compression
